title: Perp-Neg: negatives that do not fight the prompt

questions.q: Which part of the negative does Perp-Neg remove?
options: The part at right angles to the positive
questions.answer: The part at right angles to the positive
questions.why: perp = neg minus its projection on pos, and only perp is subtracted.

questions.q: When positive and negative overlap almost completely, plain cfg at 7 goes how far along the positive, in the lab?
options: About 1, because the two nearly cancel
questions.answer: About 1, because the two nearly cancel
questions.why: The table's first row has plain at 1.00, while Perp-Neg stays at 7.00.

questions.q: How many predictions per step does PerpNegGuider usually cost?
questions.why: Guider_PerpNeg.predict_noise passes all three to calc_cond_batch.

options: Plain cfg against the empty prompt, with the negative not run
questions.answer: Plain cfg against the empty prompt, with the negative not run
questions.why: With perp times 0, D = empty + cfg times (pos). The guider also sets negative_cond to None.

questions.q: A negative dead opposite to the positive gives Perp-Neg what extra push?
options: None: it has no right-angle part
questions.answer: None: it has no right-angle part
questions.why: At 180 degrees the sideways part is 0, and it stays at 7.00 while plain reaches 13.00.

questions.q: Why might comparing batch size 1 with batch size 4 mislead here?
options: The dot product sums across the whole batch, so images affect each other's split
questions.answer: The dot product sums across the whole batch, so images affect each other's split
questions.why: The source's torch.mul(neg, pos).sum() has no per-image dimension. The lab shows it.
